content.user_title: Manage Google Calendar with the gws CLI
content.value_statement: Calendar administration often requires precise API methods and parameters. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Google Calendar operations using the gws CLI.
actual_capabilities: Guides retrieval and management of calendar lists and calendar metadata.
Documents methods for creating, reading, updating, importing, moving, listing, and deleting events.
Covers access control rule creation, inspection, updates, watches, and deletion.
Supports free and busy queries across selected calendars.
Documents Calendar settings, colors, resource watches, and channel cleanup.
Directs users to inspect method schemas before building parameters and request data.
limitations: Requires the gws CLI and valid Google Workspace authentication.
Depends on the shared skill for authentication, global flags, and security rules.
Provides a method overview, while detailed parameters must come from gws schema output.
Destructive operations require careful user review before execution.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a personal schedule
use_cases.description: Review upcoming events, inspect calendar details, and create or update appointments.

use_cases.title: Plan team availability
use_cases.description: Query free and busy data before proposing meeting times across several calendars.

use_cases.title: Administer calendar resources
use_cases.description: Inspect access rules, calendar metadata, settings, and change watches for managed calendars.

prompt_templates.title: Review upcoming events
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my next ten events across all calendars. Inspect the relevant gws schema first, then summarize each date, time, calendar, and location.

prompt_templates.title: Create a calendar event
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an event titled [title] on [calendar] from [start] to [end]. Show the proposed details and request confirmation before creating it.

prompt_templates.title: Find a shared meeting time
prompt_templates.prompt: Check availability for [calendars] between [start] and [end]. Suggest three open [duration]-minute times without exposing unrelated event details.

prompt_templates.title: Audit calendar access and watches
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect access rules and active resource watches for [calendar]. Summarize owners, permissions, and watch scope before proposing any changes.

output_examples.input: Find a 30-minute opening for three calendars tomorrow afternoon.
output_examples.output: All three calendars are available from 14:00 to 14:30 and from 16:00 to 16:30. No event details were exposed.

output_examples.input: Review access to the Finance calendar.
output_examples.output: The calendar has one owner, two editors, and six viewers. No changes were made, and confirmation is required before modifying access.

best_practices: Inspect the method schema before supplying parameters or request data.
Confirm calendar identifiers, time zones, and date ranges before changing events.
Request explicit approval before deleting events, clearing calendars, or changing access rules.
anti_patterns: Do not clear a primary calendar when only one event should be removed.
Do not expose event details when a free and busy result is sufficient.
Do not use a service account as the calendar owner when another user should own the calendar.

faq.question: What setup does this skill require?
faq.answer: Install the gws CLI and configure Google Workspace authentication through the shared prerequisite skill.

faq.question: Can this skill create and update events?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents event insertion, quick addition, patching, updating, importing, and moving.

faq.question: Can this skill delete calendar data?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers event deletion, secondary calendar deletion, and primary calendar clearing, so confirmation is important.

faq.question: Can it check availability without reading event details?
faq.answer: Yes. The free and busy query returns availability for selected calendars.

faq.question: Can it manage calendar access?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents listing, reading, creating, updating, watching, and deleting access control rules.

faq.question: Where do method parameters come from?
faq.answer: Use the gws schema command for the selected resource and method before preparing parameters and request data.
